scope: Bounded read-only comparison of saved kernel8 final dmesg, stock/Merlin #1 fallback boot, and earlier custom #6 boot. No SSH, device operations, or source changes.
verdict: No newly introduced fatal kernel fault found in these captures. The requested AP/BP3/regulatory error families already occur in the stock fallback. This is not a warning-free boot, and successful radio-up state does not validate every virtual BSS.

kernel8.linux_version: Linux version 4.19.294 (leon@be19000ai) (gcc version 10.3.0 (Buildroot 2021.02.4)) #8 SMP PREEMPT Sat Oct 3 12:00:00 UTC 2026

stock_fallback.linux_version: Linux version 4.19.294 (merlin@ubuntu-dev2) (gcc version 10.3.0 (Buildroot 2021.02.4)) #1 SMP PREEMPT Wed Sep 23 15:47:28 EDT 2026

kernel6.linux_version: Linux version 4.19.294 (leon@be19000ai) (gcc version 10.3.0 (Buildroot 2021.02.4)) #6 SMP PREEMPT Sat Oct 3 12:00:00 UTC 2026

findings.observation: Both kernel8 and the stock fallback contain exactly four AP Bring up failed messages: bssidx 1 twice and bssidx 2 twice, each following bss-up return -1. The sequence appears during virtual interface initialization. The earlier kernel6 capture has none.
findings.assessment: The stock reproduction prevents attributing this error to the kernel8 PSI changes. Kernel6 absence alone does not isolate a cause because these are separate boots and captures, not a controlled configuration/timing comparison.
findings.remaining_concern: A failed virtual BSS is a real unresolved signal even when all three physical radios report up. These captures do not map each bssidx to the configured Guest/IoT SSID or prove its eventual recovery. Check per-BSS enabled/up/beacon/client status if a specific SSID is missing; do not claim all virtual networks are verified.

findings.observation: All three contain Direct firmware load for regulatory.db failed with error -2, followed by cfg80211 failed to load regulatory.db.
findings.assessment: This missing cfg80211 database is not newly introduced by kernel8. The logs alone do not establish the effective proprietary firmware country/channel policy or prove correct operation on every legal channel; do not describe the missing file as fixed or categorically harmless.

findings.observation: Each capture has Cannot open /etc/licenses, Failed to load default development license, and three OUI mismatch messages. Each then loads licenses 1119 and 1212, reports BP3 status - provisioned, and reports HTOA license present twice.
findings.assessment: The default-license/OUI messages are pre-existing failed candidate-loading paths followed by positive provisioning evidence, not evidence that kernel8 lost the active BP3/HTOA license. This is a log-based conclusion, not a complete acceleration benchmark.

findings.observation: Event-buffer/CAC setup failures, unsupported OCV, IGMP send failures and scan/deauthorize messages have baseline examples. CFG80211-ERROR prefixes also wrap informational-looking Enter, connection and supplied-MAC messages, so prefix counts alone overstate failed operations.
findings.new_exact_text_check: Only two exact CFG80211 header-plus-next-line blocks in kernel8 were absent from the union of these two baseline captures: connection channel=36 for a previously seen peer, and a disconnect event on wl1 rather than the kernel6 wl2. The operation/error families themselves are present in baseline; peer/channel/interface variation does not establish a new kernel defect.
findings.remaining_concern: The final log contains an AiMesh peer disconnect and eth0 bridge disable/reenable transitions. Later saved state reports link UP, but this short boot capture is not a long-run proof against intermittent link or client issues.

findings.assessment: The kernel6-only external copper PHY/Serdes link-up warning is absent from the current kernel8 and fallback captures. No inference that kernel8 fixed an intermittent PHY condition is justified.

findings.search_expression: Kernel panic|\bOops:|\bBUG:|WARNING: CPU:|Unable to handle kernel|Call trace:|soft lockup|hard LOCKUP|rcu.*stall|INFO: task.*blocked for more than
findings.assessment: No panic, real Oops, BUG, CPU warning backtrace, kernel access fault, call trace or explicit lockup/stall marker matched. oops_mmc is the crash-capture module name, not an Oops report. Proprietary/out-of-tree module taint lines are present and must not be conflated with crashes.

positive_live_evidence.ai_link: eth.ai UP/LOWER_UP and 2/2 successful ping responses to the internal AI board
positive_live_evidence.aimesh_agent: cfg_client running; RE_MODE=1 and configured master retained
positive_live_evidence.wired: network-first shows eth0 UP/LOWER_UP and a two-member 802.3ad bond, both members up with zero recorded link failures
positive_live_evidence.browser_observation: Parent separately reported real link rates and one 6 GHz client in Chrome. Not independently inspected by this saved-log audit; do not use as proof for all virtual BSSs.

limitations: Different boot capture lengths and configuration/timing may affect message counts.
All three radios up is a radio-level check; per-SSID success remains unverified by these files.
No long-duration load or roaming test is implied.
recommended_summary: Kernel8 is running and no new fatal kernel fault was found. Stock also emits the same AP bring-up, regulatory.db and BP3 messages; BP3 then provisions successfully. Retain a separate investigation for virtual Guest/IoT BSS startup instead of calling the log warning-free.
